liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (3 reviews): Reviewer hears The Other One as ferociously heavy, comparable to heavy metal for 1968; Once Bob comes in midway through The Other One, Jerry pushes the playing over the edge [12][14][16]
- **Feedback** (2 reviews): Reviewer found the Feedback section thoughtful and effective; The feedback segment is singled out as especially sweet [9][10]
- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): Jerry's jam in Dark Star beginning around 8:30 is picked out as awesome; Dark Star is rated top-notch [14][16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Intro/Dark Star**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-11-01.131661.sbd.restore.droncit.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 67 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Right track was very noisy and found to be mono, suggesting a soundboard problem; aggressive noise filtering was applied [1]
- **gd68-11-01.sbd.cotsman.18100.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 57 min; rated 3.29/5 by 17 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording has a rough stretch running from the Alligator through to the Alligator reprise; Soundboard mix puts Jerry up front, so his guitar's analog feedback and harmonics sound as if heard beside his amp; New Potato Caboose through Alligator, Drums and Alligator reprise is called worthless and unlistenable; skip from Cryptical Envelopment to Caution [2][9][11][15][16]
- **gd1968-11-01.sbd.kaplan.20008.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 67 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: New Potato Caboose through Feedback has a severely attenuated signal, initially almost inaudible, lasting 14:03 in total [3]
- **gd1968-11-01.sbd.kaplan.17080.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 53 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [4]. Said about its sound: Bob is nearly inaudible in stretches of Dark Star and the first five minutes of The Other One, though the recording is sublime; Signal collapses 0:41 into New Potato Caboose, stays unusable for 14:03, then returns at proper strength for the final 19:54 [4][14]

## Around the show

- Garcia is clearly heard announcing this as the Dead's last set of the evening before Alligator starts [1]
- The night balanced the raw intensity of the band's 1968 shows with the polish of 1969 [10]
- Reviewer prefers this show's sound over other copies of it on the Internet Archive [15]
- Another copy, Kaplan 20008, contains more of the Caution than this one does [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-11-01.131661.sbd.restore.droncit.flac16**: transferred by droncit; source: This is a restoration/rework using shnid 18100 (Cotsman) and 09580 (Axelrod); Diamond Cut Forensics versions 8.5 and Alpha 9 for the editing. [1]
- **gd68-11-01.sbd.cotsman.18100.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Litfin, Jim Powell, J. Barnes, and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: That portion came from the J. Powell/J. Barnes SHN seed, patched into a different source with somewhat more hiss [2]
- **gd1968-11-01.sbd.kaplan.20008.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by MSR > R > D > CD by Jim Powell. EAC > SHN by J.Barnes. Track 5a edited by Seth Kaplan; source: MSR > R > D > CD > EAC (secure) > SHN [3]. Also: Both channels of the quiet section were amplified 40 dB in Cool Edit 2000, with hiss and artifacts reduced [3]
- **gd1968-11-01.sbd.kaplan.17080.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jim Powell and J Barnes; source: MSR > R > D > CD [4]. Also: Tape has two segments: 35:02 from the last-set introduction into New Potato, and 32:14 from mid-Alligator to the end [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Ken Greenburg Grateful Dead: [1968-11-01 Silver Dollar Fairgrounds, Chico, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1968-11-01-silver-dollar-fairgrounds-chico-ca-usa/) [21]
